q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for **August 26, 2026**. Today is August 19, 2026. This means **7 days remain** until the guidance is officially released. This is an extremely tight timeframe — the question resolves in one week.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already issued forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%** (i.e., a range of approximately $89.18–$92.82 billion).

This is the official guidance the company provided and will report against on August 26, 2026. With only 7 days remaining, the guidance will be formally announced and confirmed in the earnings release itself. The question asks what guidance *will be* in the release, and that guidance has already been publicly stated.

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA confirms or slightly adjusts from the $91.0 billion guidance. Given that:
- The guidance was recently issued (May 20, 2026)
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue was $81.6 billion
- Analyst consensus clusters around $91–93.5 billion
- There is no indication in the research of any material change or withdrawal of guidance

The company will almost certainly reiterate or confirm the $91.0 billion guidance (±2%, so roughly $89.2–$92.8 billion).

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Unexpected negative business developments** in the 3+ months since guidance was issued (late May to August) — e.g., weaker demand signals, supply chain disruptions, or geopolitical/regulatory surprises affecting data center or AI deployments.
- **Macro deterioration** that significantly impacts customer capex plans in the final weeks before earnings.
- **China export controls or regulatory changes** that weren't anticipated in May guidance.

However, with only 7 days left and guidance already in the market, a major downward revision would be highly unusual and surprising.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-expected demand** in late Q2, particularly for H100/H200 GPUs in data center, potentially driven by accelerated AI adoption.
- **Upside surprise from cloud customers** or other segments not fully reflected in the May guidance.
- **Forex tailwinds** improving converted revenue from international sales.

Again, a major upward surprise would require significant positive developments since May that weren't anticipated. This is less likely than a confirmation.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **NVIDIA's official Q2 FY2027 guidance (issued May 20, 2026): $91.0 billion ±2%** = approximately $89.18–$92.82 billion
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion
- Analyst consensus estimates: ranging from $86.84 billion (LSEG average) to $93.5 billion (some aggregators), with Hudson Labs citing $91.846 billion

Companies typically revise guidance only when there are material changes to business outlook. With 7 days to the earnings date and no reported material change, NVIDIA will almost certainly stick with or modestly adjust the $91.0B guidance.

---

## Reasoning on the range

The question's range is $99.5–$115.5 billion. This is **well above** NVIDIA's official guidance of $91.0B ±2%. 

The guidance itself sits near the lower end of the provided range. For the outcome to fall in the upper half of this range (say, $107.5B+), NVIDIA would need to raise guidance by roughly **18%** from the May statement — an enormous and highly unlikely move with only 7 days notice and no material positive surprises reported in the research.

My estimate focuses on the ~$89–$93 billion band where official guidance and consensus lie:

---

Low (10th percentile): 88500000000
Median (50th percentile): 91000000000
High (90th percentile): 92800000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, is **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**. This outlook explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026).

This guidance is well above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion according to LSEG [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). Analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is generally aligned with NVIDIA's guidance, with Hudson Labs citing a consensus of $91.846 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors) and other aggregators pegging it nearer $93.5 billion [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026). The company reported a record revenue of $81.6 billion for Q1 FY2027, which ended April 26, 2026 [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). The Q2 FY2027 earnings report is scheduled for August 26, 2026 [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors).
